name: Alaska
facts: Alaska is the largest US state by area.
Denali, in Alaska, is the tallest mountain in North America.

name: Arizona
facts: The Grand Canyon, in northern Arizona, was carved by the Colorado River.
Saguaro cacti in Arizona's Sonoran Desert can grow over 40 feet tall.

name: California
facts: California has more people than any other US state.
Coast redwoods in California are the tallest trees in the world.

name: Colorado
facts: Colorado joined the US in 1876, 100 years after the Declaration of Independence.
Denver is called the Mile High City because it sits about one mile above sea level.

name: Hawaii
facts: Hawaii is the only US state made up entirely of islands.
Hawaii's islands were built by volcanoes, and Kilauea is one of the most active on Earth.

name: Idaho
facts: Idaho grows more potatoes than any other state.
Hells Canyon, on the Idaho-Oregon border, is the deepest river gorge in North America.

name: Montana
facts: Montana's Treasure State nickname comes from its gold and silver mines.
Part of Yellowstone National Park is in Montana.

name: Nevada
facts: Nevada became a state during the Civil War, which is why its flag says Battle Born.
Hoover Dam stands on the Colorado River at the Nevada-Arizona border.

name: New Mexico
facts: Santa Fe is the highest state capital in the US, at about 7,000 feet.
Carlsbad Caverns in New Mexico has a huge underground chamber called the Big Room.

name: Oregon
facts: Crater Lake in Oregon is the deepest lake in the United States.
The American beaver is Oregon's state animal.

name: Utah
facts: Utah has five national parks.
The Great Salt Lake is the largest salt lake in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Washington
facts: Washington is the only state named after a US president.
Mount Rainier is the tallest mountain in Washington.

name: Wyoming
facts: Yellowstone, mostly in Wyoming, became the world's first national park in 1872.
Wyoming gave women the right to vote in 1869, long before the rest of the country.
